channels.title: Built in Time
channels.meta_description:
What did your city look like 300 years ago?

We rebuild cities in 3D and play their entire history in minutes. One camera. One skyline. Every year from the first settlement to today, and sometimes beyond.

Watch forts become towns, railroads arrive, skyscrapers race upward, landmarks rise and fall, and the city you know take shape year by year.

New city every week. Subscribe and tell us which city we should rebuild next.

Every video is an illustrative 3D reconstruction built from historical maps, open city data and published histories, not archival footage.

channels.title: Historia de Ciudades
channels.meta_description:
Historia de ciudades contada a través de documentales sobre su origen, auge, poder, conflictos, caída y transformación.

Detrás de cada gran avenida, monumento y rascacielos existe una historia de ambición, riqueza, progreso y personas que tuvieron que pagar el precio.

En Historia de Ciudades reconstruimos cómo nacieron las ciudades que cambiaron el mundo, quiénes las hicieron poderosas, qué abusos ocurrieron durante su crecimiento, por qué algunas terminaron en decadencia y cómo viven en la actualidad.

Desde antiguas ciudades mineras hasta grandes metrópolis modernas, exploramos la historia urbana, económica y humana que normalmente no aparece en las postales.

Aquí no solo contemplamos ciudades: descubrimos quiénes las levantaron, quiénes se quedaron con la riqueza y qué consecuencias quedaron enterradas bajo sus calles.

Suscríbete y conoce la verdadera historia de las grandes ciudades del mundo.

channels.title: CityEons
channels.meta_description:
Watch the world's great cities and regions change - from their earliest settlements to today.

I'm Eric, and CityEons is my personal passion project. With a background in History from the University of Greifswald, I combine my love of the past with 3D visualization to bring history to life.

I create cinematic timelapses of cities rising, expanding, burning and rebuilding—and of entire regions, like Europe from the Bronze Age to the present day.

Each reconstruction starts with real geodata - terrain, rivers, streets and buildings - and draws on historical maps, archaeology, population records and other sources. I carefully research dates and figures, and model landmarks to real-world dimensions wherever possible.

In just a few minutes, you can watch centuries or even millennia unfold before your eyes.

No AI imagery. No narration. Just places, years and music - in 4K.

It all started with London. Many more cities and regions are to come.

channels.title: Stratapolis
channels.meta_description:
Cities through the millennia: thousands of years of one city in a single continuous shot.

Each Stratapolis film follows one city from its first settlement to today. Walls rise, quarters fill in, rivers shift, empires change hands. The maps are built in Blender from real terrain, land-cover and OpenStreetMap data at true scale, the cities are reconstructed in 3D, every card is based on sources, and each film has its own original music.

Every film is a different city, from ancient capitals to cities still growing today. All films are in the playlist Cities Through Time.

Historic city extents, walls and vanished buildings are illustrative reconstructions based on the sources, not archaeological plans. Sources and licences are listed in every video description.

Which city should come next? Suggest it in the comments.

channels.title: Forma Urbis - Not In A Day
channels.meta_description:
Forma Urbis — Not in a Day.

Watch real cities grow, building by building, from the year they were first accurately mapped to today.

Every film begins on the city's first measured map, laid out on the ground in 3D. From there the city rises year by year, built from official records: when each building went up, its footprint and how many floors it has. Walls fall, rivers move, harbours spread and suburbs swallow the fields.

We don't invent the past. We start where reliable records start, and anything we had to reconstruct is marked "estimated" on screen and in the description. No AI-generated imagery.

The name comes from the Forma Urbis Romae, the great marble map of ancient Rome carved around 203–211 AD. Rome wasn't built in a day. Neither was any other city.

Data: national cadastres (such as Spain's Dirección General del Catastro) and © OpenStreetMap contributors.

Which city should rise next? Tell us in the comments.

channels.title: City Ages
channels.meta_description:
Watch the world's great cities grow, century by century, in 3D.

Every City Ages film follows one city from its first settlement to today, seen from above on its real map. The rivers and streets are where they really are, and you can watch fires, plagues, wars and railways reshape them as the years count up.

No narration and no filler: just the city, the dates and the music. Each film has chapters, so you can jump straight to the moment you care about.

How it's made: the maps and building footprints come from OpenStreetMap, the landmarks are modelled by hand, and every frame is rendered in 3D. No AI-generated images. We model how each city grew from historical sources, so treat the films as visual reconstructions rather than exact surveys.

First up: London, AD 40 to 2026.

New cities every two weeks. Subscribe and tell us which city should be next.

channels.title: Measured Cities
channels.meta_description:
How cities grew, measured. Each video builds one real city in 3D on its own terrain, from the first settlement to today, with the numbers on screen: population, built-up area and the source of every figure.

We start with Edinburgh: from a hill fort on Castle Rock around the year 600 to the city of 2026. Fast-growing megacities like Jakarta and Lagos come next.

Built-up area: GHSL (European Commission JRC). Population: UN World Urbanization Prospects and historic records (early figures marked "est."). Today's buildings: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Terrain: Copernicus DEM. The 3D buildings are illustrative; the numbers are measured.

Music only, no narration. New cities regularly.
